newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends down, San Onofre nukes back.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends down, San Onofre nukes back.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Monday as both units at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) in southern California were in process of returning to full output.
Southern California Edison Co (SoCal Edison) said the 1,080 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 3 in southern California, resumed electricity production early Monday.
Restart of SONGS 3 was delayed to Sunday from Friday due to a water contamination in the unit's lube oil system.

The adjacent 1,070 MW unit 2 stayed near 70 percent of capacity during maintenance work on a main feedwater pump, dashing hope of some players that SoCal Edison would need to shut it to complete the pump repairs.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down $1.36 at $35.25 a megawatt hour after hitting a low of $35.25.
September PV finished down 55 cents at $28.56 after bouncing between $28.40 and $28.70. Deferred PV contracts ended 25 to 40 cents lower.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down 72 cents at $21.18 a MWh, just three cents above its session low.
September COB finished down 47 cents at $21.72. Other COB months ended 10 to 45 cents lower.
More spot supply from other western power units also put downward pressure on futures prices, market sources said.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Washington, reached full power as of early Monday.
Also, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada was restarted slightly ahead of schedule late Friday night after tripping off line a week ago.

Firm, peak power prices for Tuesday at PV slipped to $36.00-41.00 a MWh from Friday's $39.00-44.00 for today. Tuesday power sold at COB firmed 75 cents to $17.00-18.00 after Bonneville Power Administration withheld sales of next-day peak electricity.
Market sources said futures and cash prices would come under pressure again Tuesday amid rising spot supply.
Separately, the Western Systems Coordinating Council was scheduled to vote this week whether to raise capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission system to 6,900 MW frm 6,300 MW.
Six-to-ten day forecasts called for cooler than normal summer weather in the Northwest and along the California coast and seasonal temperatures in the interior section of the Southwest.
NYMEX estimated 568 COB and 603 PV contracts were sold.
